motion.name: roll-step

motion.purpose: Rolling cells swap glyphs without animating leaves; only the final character lands with a real flip.

motion.name: spin-blur
motion.purpose: Applied to the inner character only. The housing is fixed hardware and stays sharp.

motion.name: reduced-motion

motion.purpose: The panicking column is exactly what a reduced-motion user switched off. The countdown itself keeps running.

narrative.overview:
One room, two materials. A painted institutional wall fills the viewport; a dark split-flap departure board is bolted into it with four visible screws. Nothing floats and nothing is decorative for its own sake: every gradient in the build is either the sheen of enamel paint, the recess of a panel into a wall, the bevel of a flap leaf, or the shadow one leaf throws on the one below it. The system is a photograph of hardware, not a UI theme.

Density is extreme in one direction only. The countdown digits are enormous, far past the usual 6rem display ceiling, because the product is a single number and the reference device is a phone in a chat app's in-app browser. Everything else — the departure rail, the unit captions, the departed-service note — is small, wide-tracked uppercase running along the board's edges, the way real station signage labels its own hardware. Colour is withheld almost entirely: institutional green holds the wall, near-black holds the board, bone ink carries the characters, and one signal orange-red appears on exactly one line.

The build has no interactive control of any kind. There is no button, no link, no field, no navigation. Reflow of the board and the enormous number is the entire interface. A second surface exists: the 1200×630 link-preview frame, which is not a crop of the page but its own composition, with its own type sizes and its own visible sentence.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials only: enamel wall and recessed dark board.
One accent (signal red-orange), one line of it, ever.
Uppercase, wide-tracked, tabular Archivo Narrow throughout.
Every depth cue drawn from a single black/white alpha ramp.
All geometry calc()ed off one per-unit cell variable.
No interactive control; nothing hovers, nothing is clickable-looking.

rules.name: The One-Ramp Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn exclusively from shade-0…shade-5 and sheen-0…sheen-3. A new shadow, bevel, or hairline picks the nearest existing step and never introduces a fresh alpha. If nothing on the ramp fits, the effect is wrong, not the ramp.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule (v2: signal marks what you missed)
rules.body: The signal colour marks what is gone — the departed service, and now also the wrong answer. Never for emphasis or decoration, and it appears in only one place per screen. The correct answer never gets green; the wall already owns green, and a second instance would read as a second material, not a second meaning. Correctness is announced by material instead: a flap cell flips to a fully-lit --ink fill (dark glyph on bone), the inverse of every other cell. Every answer state also carries a glyph (check or cross), never colour or brightness alone.

rules.name: The Board-Ink Rule (--ink-3 is a colour on the board, not on the wall)
rules.body: The three ink tints are calibrated against --board, not --enamel. On the board --ink-3 is ~7:1 and is the correct quietest step: rail keys, unit captions, the stimulus label, the source citation, a disabled button. On the wall the same tint is 3,38:1 — a fail for the small tracked uppercase it is always used for, and all of v2 chrome (view tabs, section captions, stat captions, hints, the countdown signage line) stands on the wall. There the quietest legible step is --ink-2 (5,39:1) and that is the floor. No new tint bridges the gap: the ramp was never wrong, the surface was. The check is mechanical — if the painted background is --enamel, --ink-3 is not available.

rules.name: The Metal Is Not Ink Rule
rules.body: Screws and axle pins draw from the hardware tokens, not from the ink tints. Anything that is supposed to be a physical fastener is grey-green metal with a two-stop gradient and a shade-4 seat shadow.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every numeral in the build sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. At 100 updates per second, proportional figures make the layout twitch. This is correctness, not polish.

rules.name: The All-Caps Signage Rule (v2: signage governs chrome, not content)
rules.body: Chrome — rails, tabs, unit captions, section headings, source citations, the departed-service note — stays uppercase with 0.14-0.22em tracking. v2 puts prose on the board for the first time (a question, a reading passage, an option) and verzalky on multi-line prose proved unreadable against real Testovanie 9 items, so content is now a sentence: lower case, tracking 0, line-height 1.5, in four new roles (body, option, answer, stat). If a real board would stencil it onto hardware, it is signage; if a person wrote it to be read, it is content.

rules.name: The Cell-Derived Type Rule
rules.body: Flap type size, line height, pin diameter, and spin blur are all calc() expressions on --c. Never hard-code a font size inside a flap; change --c and the whole unit rescales correctly.

rules.name: The No-Scroll Rule (v2: chrome doesn't scroll, content does)
rules.body: The original rule still governs the countdown itself: #/tabula and ?og=1 never scroll, and cell size stays bounded by min(vw, vh). The game cannot hold to the stricter form — a reading passage plus a table plus four options does not fit 667px tall, and shrinking to fit would make the text illegible. Now two tiers: chrome is pinned (corner countdown and progress strip are position:sticky at the top, never leave the viewport); content scrolls (question body, passage, and options move under that chrome like a normal document).

rules.name: The Per-View Countdown Rule
rules.body: The countdown is never absent, but its register changes with the screen job. The flap strip costs 117px of a 667px phone — 18% of the viewport. On #/dnes, #/vysledok and #/vykaz that is money well spent: the countdown is the emotional motor and nothing there competes for reading space. On #/uloha the same 117px is what pushed the answer options off the screen, in exchange for a number that does not change during a question — so there the countdown is a sign, not hardware: one signage line, label role, ~30px, "TESTOVANIE 9 · 196 DNÍ", sharing the pinned band with the progress strip and linking to #/tabula. Day granularity; nobody reads minutes on a screen they stand on for ninety seconds. #/tabula keeps the full five-unit board unchanged.

rules.name: The Sticky-Stimulus Rule (open once, then a pinned line)
rules.body: A question sharing a reading passage with its siblings keeps that passage position:sticky at the top of its panel. The goal is unchanged: the passage must be reachable at the fourth question of the group, because an ungrounded question is worse than an unscrolled one. The means are not "keep it open". The stimulus is a native <details>: open at the group first question, and from the second question a single pinned 44px summary row (UKÁŽKA · ZIMNÉ PARALYMPIJSKÉ HRY ⌄) that opens on tap. Native <details> and not a scripted panel, because keyboard operation, focus ring and screen-reader announcement all come free. Open, it is still capped at max-height:36dvh with its own internal scroll and a shade-only fade at its bottom edge — an uncapped multi-section passage (ZPH ran past 900px) would replace the question with the reading. Governing measurement: at 375×667 with the stimulus collapsed or absent, the question and every option are visible without scrolling (last option row ends 39px above the thumb bar, document 670px against a 667px viewport). With the stimulus open the page scrolls, and that is allowed.

rules.name: The Reflow-Not-Shrink Rule
rules.body: When horizontal space runs out, units move to a new row. They do not scale down. The number is the product; it never gives up size to fit a layout.

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit in the wall, not on it. New panels get an outline plus inset shadow; a drop shadow is only ever the few pixels that seat an object against its substrate. No lifted cards, no hover elevation.

rules.name: The Fixed-Cell Rule
rules.body: Character cells never resize to their content. Text is padded into a fixed cell count; empty cells stay visible as blank housings. That is what a mechanical board does and it is the strongest single signal of the world.

rules.name: The Two-Surface Rule
rules.body: The page and the 1200×630 link-preview frame are two different compositions from one document, switched by a body.og class: fixed 56/92/34px cells, a narrower board, a tighter column gap, and the sentence made visible. The preview frame is never treated as a crop of the page. Anything that only makes sense once a viewer has arrived belongs on the page; anything that has to work in a chat list, with the board tiny and the digits blurred, belongs in the frame.

rules.name: The Blurred-Digits Rule
rules.body: The preview frame shows no readable time value. The time field is filled with blurred non-numeric glyphs, because a static image would lie about the number every day after it was generated. Remaining time appears in the preview only as whole days, in og:description, rewritten by the daily cron.

rules.name: The Housing-Is-Fixed Rule
rules.body: Motion blur is applied to the inner character element, never to the cell. The housing is bolted hardware and is always sharp; only the character moves.

dos: Do derive every flap dimension from --c with calc() — glyph size (1.44), cell height (1.55), pin diameter (.085), spin blur (.026 / .05).
Do pull every shadow, bevel, and hairline from the shade/sheen ramp; pick the nearest existing step.
Do set tabular-nums on anything numeric.
Do re-check 375×667 after any change to cell sizing, board padding, or column gaps.
Do keep uppercase and 0.14–0.22em tracking on every string outside a flap cell.
Do treat the preview frame as its own surface with its own type sizes.
Do keep the wall a single flat green with material supplied by grain, sheen, and vignette.
Do write question, passage, option, and answer text in sentence case — signage governs chrome, not content, as of v2.
Do pin the corner countdown and progress strip; let everything else scroll.
Do cap a sticky stimulus's height with its own internal scroll — never let it grow to fill the viewport.
Do carry the streak's record and reserve on the same line as the live streak, so the record is never one tap from a broken streak.
Check anything standing on --enamel against --ink-2 as its darkest ink; --ink-3 is a board colour.
Collapse a sticky stimulus to its 44px summary row from the group second question on.
Re-measure 375×667 on #/uloha after any change to the pinned band — question plus all options on one screen is a number, not a feeling.
donts: Don't introduce a new rgba value for a shadow. If no ramp step fits, the effect is wrong.
Don't use the signal colour for anything but the departed service.
Don't shrink units to keep them on one row; reflow instead.
Don't blur, transform, or animate .flap itself — the housing never moves.
Don't let a character cell size itself to its content; pad into the fixed cell count.
Don't add lifted cards or hover elevation; surfaces are recessed into the wall.
Don't put a readable time value in the preview frame at any granularity finer than days.
Don't give screws or pins an ink colour; hardware is metal.
Don't add a build step, a dependency, or a framework — three files, served as-is.
Don't give a correct answer a green fill — correctness is material plus a glyph, never a second colour.
Don't set question, passage, or option text in uppercase — retired for content as of v2.
Don't let pointerdown anywhere in the document trigger the cascade/bell/shout once the game ships — scoped to the corner countdown tile alone.
Don't invent a new chart type for the report; the 14-day strip reuses the small Flap Cell the progress strip already uses.
Put --ink-3 on the wall. Tabs, section captions, stat captions and hints sit on --enamel, where that tint is 3,38:1 — use --ink-2, never a new tint.
Put the flap countdown on #/uloha; there it is one signage line. And never drop the countdown from a view to buy space — change its register instead.
Repeat a label a line already contains (SÉRIA over SÉRIA 9 DNÍ), or let a caption wrap away from its own number.
Say a subject was odbavený — a passenger is checked in at an airport, a train is vypravený.
